predecessors.name: Principality of Vladimir-Suzdal (Grand Principality of Vladimir)
predecessors.text: the city of Tver and the western slice of the Pereyaslavl-Zalessky patrimony, 'detached' by Yaroslav Vsevolodovich in the 1230s or 1240s

successors.name: Grand Principality of Moscow
successors.text: 'The principality stretched from Kashin in the east to Zubtsov in the west', around Tver on the upper Volga, 'approximately in the area currently occupied by Tver Oblast and the eastern part of…

ledger.x: 1246: Yaroslav Yaroslavich becomes the first prince of Tver.
ledger.cpn: Principality of Vladimir-Suzdal (Grand Principality of Vladimir)

ledger.x: 1327: the Horde, Moscow and Suzdal punish Tver's uprising.
1327: the uprising is crushed and Tver stays a principality.
1375: Tver makes peace and calls Dmitry Donskoy 'elder brother'.
12 September 1485: Ivan III's forces seize Tver.
1485: Moscow annexes the Principality of Tver, whole.
1485: the Principality of Tver ends, its land passing to the Grand Principality of Moscow ('Succeeded by: Grand Principality of Moscow', infobox).

wars.name: Tver Uprising of 1327
wars.outcome: The uprising against Ozbeg's cousin Chol-khan was crushed by a Mongol force of 50,000 led by Ivan of Moscow and Alexander of Suzdal; Tver was burned and its power reduced, with no land taken.

wars.name: Struggle between Moscow and Tver for the grand princedom of Vladimir
wars.outcome: Moscow prevailed: Tver's princes held the Vladimir patent in 1305, 1322 and 1375 but Dmitry Donskoy's treaty of 1375 made Tver his junior ('elder brother').

wars.name: Lithuanian-Muscovite War (1368-1372), Tver front
wars.outcome: Moscow invaded Tver in 1368 and again in 1370; the Tver-Moscow quarrel was settled only by the 1375 treaty.

wars.name: Muscovite conquest of Tver
wars.outcome: Ivan III's army seized Tver on 12 September 1485 and annexed the principality; its prince fled to Lithuania.

certainty.note: No page gives a treaty or survey line for Tver: 'Formerly a land of woods and bogs'; the Kashin and Zubtsov limits are approximate.
